source.document: Written for this site (not from your PDFs)

sections.title: Own your projects

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this, so this page was written for the site, as of October 2026. Tools and versions change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on details.

blocks: A fresher who can defend a project in depth is rare and memorable. Prepare each project so that you can draw it, defend it and criticise it. Your own question list is on the **Resume and project walkthroughs** step (plan day 52).

headers: Example of the level of detail
rows: Who uses it and what hurt before
Services, data stores, why this shape
What you personally designed and built: say "I"
One real bug or trade-off, and how you solved it
A measured result, and what you would change

sections.title: Fill this in for every project

rows: Access patterns and what you rejected
What happens when each dependency is down
Real or tested requests per second and data size
How do you know it works?
A specific change with its reason

blocks.title: Be honest about numbers
blocks.text: Never invent metrics: interviewers probe them. If you have none, run a load test on your project now, and quote what you measured and how.

sections.title: If your projects feel too small
blocks: Add one production-grade concern to an existing project rather than starting another CRUD app:

rows: Load test and fix a real bottleneck

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Be able to draw every project from memory.
- Say "I" for your work and "we" for the team's.
- Prepare the failure modes, not just the happy path.
- Only quote numbers you can defend.

items.question: Your project uses Kafka. What will the follow-ups be?
items.answer: Why not a simple queue or a direct call, the partition key, ordering, duplicate handling, retries, lag, and what happens when the consumer is down.

items.question: How do you answer "what was your contribution" on a team project?
items.answer: Name specific components and decisions you owned, and credit the rest to the team. Be ready to go deep on exactly what you claim.
